recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is +12.8% above baseline (72.2 vs 64.0 ms), indicating strong parasympathetic resilience
Resting HR is -5.1% below baseline (48.9 vs 51.5 bpm), supporting recovery
Recovery balance = +2.44 (HRV z-score minus load z-score), well above 0, confirming recovery is outpacing load
Sleep average is only 4.7h (vs 4.5h baseline) but 15/14 days <7h — chronic sleep debt persists despite slight improvement
readiness.guidance: The athlete is currently in a stable, trainable state — not overrecovered nor compromised — but chronic sleep deficit must be addressed before progressing intensity.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows reduced volume and pace consistency compared to last month, with notable efficiency decline and elevated aerobic TE, but improved HRV and resting HR suggest underlying physiological adaptation.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +35 spm month-over-month — the largest single change — and aligns with recent runs showing cadence >157 spm during longer efforts, suggesting intentional neuromuscular focus or fatigue-driven shortening of stride.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month’s volume would require ~55.3 km across 8 sessions (~6.9 km/session) in 19 days — unsustainable given chronic sleep debt (15/14 days <7h) and current recovery balance being driven by low load rather than robust recovery capacity; chasing this number risks reinforcing poor sleep habits and diminishing returns.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with worsening running economy
insights.body: Despite improved HRV and resting HR, running economy recently spiked to 253.5 ml/kg/km (rating: 'Recreational') — the highest in the recent series — while sleep remains persistently low (4.7h avg, 15/14 days <7h); literature links sub-6h sleep to 3–5% reduction in metabolic efficiency, consistent with the observed 0.26-unit efficiency decline this month.

insights.title: Lower acute load coincides with improved aerobic decoupling
insights.body: This month’s ACWR (0.9) and acute load (233) are the lowest in 4 weeks, and latest aerobic decoupling is 4.8% — the first sub-5% value in 6 runs — suggesting reduced fatigue allows better maintenance of efficiency across duration.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance masks inefficiency at threshold
insights.body: Zone 3 comprises 43% of this month’s training (vs 29% last month), yet efficiency in Z3 (0.7516 m/beat) is lower than Z2 (0.7901 m/beat) and Z4 (0.7582 m/beat), indicating disproportionate time spent at intensities where economy is weakest — likely contributing to elevated aerobic TE (2.5) and reduced endurance sustainability.

insights.title: Cadence surge reflects form adaptation — not fatigue
insights.body: Cadence rose from 118 spm (Jul) to 153 spm (Aug), with recent long run (12.0 km) at 157 spm and ground contact time dropping from 301 ms (Aug 9) to 299 ms (Aug 13), while vertical oscillation increased slightly (7.8 → 8.0) — consistent with active, efficient turnover rather than compensatory shuffling.

recommendations.action: Zone 2 run: 6.0 km, HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥155 spm, on Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Maintains neuromuscular gains from recent cadence focus while staying safely below lactate threshold (Z3 starts at ~138–140 bpm for this athlete), supporting aerobic base without adding stress

recommendations.action: Complete 3 nights of ≥6.5h sleep before any Zone 3 session; log sleep start/end times daily
recommendations.reason: Chronic sleep debt (15/14 days <7h) directly impairs running economy and recovery capacity — this is the highest-leverage intervention to restore efficiency and decoupling resilience

recommendations.action: One 20-min Zone 1 walk or mobility session (no HR monitor needed) on Thursday, focusing on hip flexor + calf release
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time remains >298 ms across all recent runs — modest mobility work supports stride efficiency without loading the nervous system

risk_flags.evidence: 15 of last 14 days with <7h sleep; running economy deteriorated to 253.5 ml/kg/km (‘Recreational’ rating)
risk_flags.action: Prioritize sleep hygiene and bedtime consistency before increasing volume or intensity

risk_flags.evidence: Zone 3 now 43% of monthly volume (up from 29% in July), yet Z3 efficiency (0.7516 m/beat) is lowest among all zones except Z5
risk_flags.action: Reduce Zone 3 share to ≤30% and shift 10% to Zone 2 to improve aerobic efficiency and reduce TE drift

weekly_focus.theme: Consolidate aerobic efficiency through sleep-supported neuromuscular control
weekly_focus.description: Leverage current adequate readiness to reinforce cadence gains and restore running economy — not by adding load, but by anchoring form improvements in rested physiology.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run with cadence target
Short Zone 1+2 mixed-effort run emphasizing rhythm and relaxation
